drinks.title: Bijou
drinks.description: The Bijou is a classic cocktail that dates back to the late 19th century. Its name, meaning 'jewel' in French, reflects the drink's vibrant colors and luxurious ingredients. The cocktail is a harmonious blend of gin, green Chartreuse, and sweet vermouth, accented with a dash of orange bitters. Traditionally served in a cocktail glass, the Bijou is garnished with a lemon twist or cherry, adding a touch of elegance to its presentation. This sophisticated drink is perfect for those who appreciate complex flavors and a touch of history in their cocktails.

drinks.title: Zombie
drinks.description: The Zombie is a classic tiki cocktail known for its potent mix of rums and tropical flavors. Created in the 1930s, this drink combines light rum, gold rum, and 151-proof rum with a blend of fruit juices and sweeteners, resulting in a complex and flavorful beverage. The addition of Pernod adds a unique anise flavor, while grenadine provides a touch of sweetness and color. Traditionally served in a hurricane glass, the Zombie is garnished with fruit and often enjoyed during festive occasions. Due to its high alcohol content, it's recommended to consume this cocktail responsibly.

drinks.title: Mojito
drinks.description: The Mojito is a refreshing Cuban cocktail that perfectly balances sweet, citrus, and mint flavors. Originating in Havana, this classic drink has become a beloved summer favorite worldwide. The combination of white rum, fresh lime juice, sugar, mint leaves, and soda water creates a light and invigorating beverage. The muddling of mint and sugar releases essential oils, infusing the drink with aromatic freshness. Traditionally served over crushed ice in a highball glass, the Mojito is perfect for warm days and beach gatherings.
drinks.instructions: Muddle mint leaves with sugar and lime juice. Add a splash of soda water and fill the glass with cracked ice. Pour the rum and top with soda water. Garnish with fresh mint and a lime wedge.
drinks.imageAlt: A refreshing Mojito in a highball glass with fresh mint, lime, and crushed ice.

drinks.title: Margarita
drinks.description: The Margarita is arguably the most popular tequila-based cocktail in the world. This Mexican classic perfectly balances the sharpness of tequila with the sweetness of Cointreau and the tartness of fresh lime juice. The drink is traditionally served in a glass with a salted rim, which enhances the flavors and adds a savory element. Whether blended with ice or served on the rocks, the Margarita is a versatile cocktail that has inspired countless variations, from fruity to spicy. It's the perfect drink for celebrating or relaxing with friends.
drinks.instructions: Rub the rim of the glass with the lime slice to make the salt stick to it. Take care to moisten only the outer rim and sprinkle the salt on it. Shake the tequila, Cointreau, and lime juice with ice, then strain into the glass.
drinks.imageAlt: A classic Margarita with a salted rim in a margarita glass, garnished with a lime wheel.

drinks.title: Old Fashioned
drinks.description: The Old Fashioned is one of the oldest known cocktails, dating back to the early 19th century. This timeless drink showcases the quality of the whiskey used, making it a favorite among bourbon and whiskey enthusiasts. The simple combination of whiskey, sugar, bitters, and a twist of citrus peel creates a sophisticated and balanced cocktail. The muddling of sugar with bitters creates a flavorful base, while the large ice cube slowly dilutes the drink, allowing the flavors to evolve. This drink is the epitome of classic cocktail craftsmanship.
drinks.instructions: Place sugar cube in old fashioned glass and saturate with bitters, add a dash of plain water. Muddle until dissolved. Fill the glass with ice cubes and add whiskey. Garnish with orange twist and a cocktail cherry.
drinks.imageAlt: An Old Fashioned in a rocks glass with a large ice cube, orange peel, and cherry.

drinks.title: Manhattan
drinks.description: The Manhattan is a classic cocktail that originated in New York City in the 1870s. This sophisticated drink combines whiskey with sweet vermouth and aromatic bitters, creating a smooth and complex flavor profile. The Manhattan is traditionally stirred with ice and strained into a chilled cocktail glass, then garnished with a maraschino cherry. The drink's perfect balance of sweet and bitter notes makes it a timeless favorite among cocktail enthusiasts. Whether made with bourbon or rye whiskey, the Manhattan remains a staple of American cocktail culture.
drinks.instructions: Stirred over ice, strained into a chilled glass, garnished with a cherry, and served straight up.
drinks.imageAlt: A Manhattan cocktail in a coupe glass, garnished with a maraschino cherry.

drinks.title: Negroni
drinks.description: The Negroni is an iconic Italian cocktail with a bold, bitter flavor profile. Invented in Florence in 1919, this drink combines equal parts gin, Campari, and sweet vermouth, creating a perfectly balanced aperitif. The Negroni's distinctive red color comes from the Campari, which also provides its characteristic bitter taste. This cocktail is typically served over ice in a rocks glass and garnished with an orange peel. The Negroni has experienced a resurgence in popularity in recent years and is beloved by those who appreciate complex, bittersweet flavors.
drinks.instructions: Stir into glass over ice, garnish with orange peel and serve.
drinks.imageAlt: A vibrant red Negroni in a rocks glass with ice and an orange peel garnish.

drinks.title: Daiquiri
drinks.description: The Daiquiri is a classic Cuban cocktail that showcases the beauty of simplicity. Created in the early 1900s, this drink consists of just three ingredients: white rum, fresh lime juice, and simple syrup. The Daiquiri is the perfect example of how high-quality ingredients and proper balance can create an exceptional cocktail. Traditionally served straight up in a chilled coupe glass, the Daiquiri is crisp, refreshing, and allows the quality of the rum to shine through. It's a favorite of cocktail purists and a must-know for any bartender.
drinks.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
drinks.imageAlt: A classic Daiquiri in a coupe glass with a lime wheel garnish.

drinks.title: Whiskey Sour
drinks.description: The Whiskey Sour is a classic American cocktail that dates back to the 1860s. This refreshing drink perfectly balances the boldness of whiskey with the tartness of lemon juice and the sweetness of simple syrup. The addition of egg white (optional) creates a silky texture and a beautiful foam on top of the drink. When shaken vigorously with ice, the cocktail achieves a perfect harmony of flavors and textures. Traditionally served in a rocks glass over ice or straight up in a coupe glass, the Whiskey Sour is garnished with a cherry and orange slice, making it as visually appealing as it is delicious.
drinks.instructions: Shake whiskey, lemon juice, and simple syrup with ice. If using egg white, dry shake first, then add ice and shake again. Strain into a glass filled with ice. Garnish with cherry and orange slice.
drinks.imageAlt: A Whiskey Sour in a rocks glass with a frothy top, garnished with a cherry and orange slice.

drinks.title: Cosmopolitan
drinks.description: The Cosmopolitan, or 'Cosmo,' is a modern classic that gained worldwide fame in the 1990s. This sophisticated pink cocktail combines vodka, Cointreau, cranberry juice, and fresh lime juice, creating a perfectly balanced sweet-tart flavor profile. The drink's elegant appearance and refreshing taste made it a symbol of cosmopolitan lifestyle and glamour. Served in a martini glass and garnished with a twist of orange or lemon peel, the Cosmopolitan is both visually stunning and delicious. Despite its association with a specific era, it remains a beloved choice for those who appreciate well-crafted vodka cocktails.
drinks.instructions: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into a chilled martini glass. Garnish with a twist of lemon or orange peel.
drinks.imageAlt: A pink Cosmopolitan in a martini glass with a lemon twist garnish.

drinks.title: Espresso Martini
drinks.description: The Espresso Martini is a modern classic cocktail that perfectly combines coffee and cocktails. Created in London in the 1980s, this drink features vodka, coffee liqueur, and freshly brewed espresso, shaken vigorously with ice to create a rich, frothy layer on top. The result is a smooth, energizing cocktail that's perfect for after-dinner or late-night occasions. The Espresso Martini has experienced a massive resurgence in popularity and is now one of the most requested cocktails in bars worldwide. Its combination of caffeine and alcohol makes it a unique choice for those looking for both refreshment and a boost.
drinks.instructions: Shake vodka, coffee liqueur, and freshly brewed espresso with ice until well-chilled and frothy. Strain into a chilled martini glass. Garnish with three coffee beans on top of the foam.
drinks.imageAlt: An Espresso Martini in a martini glass with a frothy layer and three coffee beans on top.

drinks.title: Piña Colada
drinks.description: The Piña Colada is the official drink of Puerto Rico and the ultimate tropical cocktail. This creamy, sweet drink combines white rum, coconut cream, and pineapple juice, blended with ice to create a frozen paradise in a glass. Created in San Juan in the 1950s, the Piña Colada has become synonymous with beach vacations and tropical getaways. The drink's rich, coconutty flavor paired with tangy pineapple makes it irresistibly refreshing. Traditionally served in a hurricane glass and garnished with pineapple and a maraschino cherry, the Piña Colada is the perfect escape cocktail.
drinks.instructions: Blend all ingredients with ice until smooth. Pour into a hurricane glass. Garnish with a pineapple wedge and maraschino cherry.

drinks.description: Vampiros may be made in a tall glass or an old fashioned glass. Bartenders may first "rim" the glass with Kosher Salt, which is done by placing a layer of Kosher Salt on a chopping board, moistening the glass' rim with lime juice or water, and then placing the upside down glass rim onto the Kosher Salt, so that the salt sticks to the moistened rim. drinks.description:
To ensure that your pork fat is just as delicious as theirs, here’s their adobo marinade and what to do with it (you’ll also need a rack of ribs):

4 ancho chiles, 8 guajillo chiles and 4 chipotle chiles, plus 4 cloves roasted garlic, half a cup of cider vinegar, a quarter teaspoon of Mexican oregano, 1 teaspoon of ground black pepper, a whole clove, a quarter teaspoon of ground cinnamon and a half teaspoon of ground cumin.

Toast the dried chiles and soak in water for at least an hour until they are rehydrated. Drain and discard the soaking liquid. Combine the soaked chiles with the remaining ingredients and purée until smooth.

Cold smoke a rack of baby back pork ribs by taking a large hotel pan with woodchips on one side and charcoal on the other. Place another, smaller, pan with pork ribs, above the charcoal/woodchip pan. Ignite the charcoal, being careful to not ignite the woodchips. Cover both pans with foil and allow to smoke for 10-15 minutes, until desired level of smoke is achieved, then coat with adobo marinade and wrap in tin foil prior to placing ribs in a 300 degree oven for 7 hours. When the ribs have cooled, strain off the fat and use for the infusion.

If you’re having a hard time coming up to the same kind of volume of fat, make up the balance with pork lard from a butcher. To get the same depth of flavor without the ribs, heat up the fat in a pot with a few spoons of the marinade.

Once you’ve got your tub of seasoned pork fat in cooled liquid form, pour equal amounts of Ilegal Joven mezcal and fat into a sealable container. Seal the container and give it a really good shake, then put it in the freezer overnight. When the whole thing is separated and congealed, pour it through a fine mesh chinoise. If you don’t have a chinoise, try a fine mesh strainer, or if you don’t have one of those, try spooning off most of the fat. There will be some beads of orange fat left in the strained mezcal: run that through a few layers of cheesecloth (or coffee filters in a pinch) to get rid of the last of it.

The mezcal is now ready for drinking, straight-up or in a cocktail. 

Habanero tincture

Slice habaneros and add 2 ounces Ilegal Joven mezcal.
Allow to sit overnight or until desired level of heat is achieved.
Cocktail

Combine mezcal and chocolate liqueur in a mixing glass with ice and stir for 45 seconds.
Strain into chilled coupe.
Carefully "sink" the coffee liqueur down the inside of the coupe over a spoon.
Garnish with 5 drops habanero tincture.

Step 1
Pour rosé into a 13x9" pan and freeze until almost solid (it won't completely solidify due to the alcohol), at least 6 hours.

Step 2
Meanwhile, bring sugar and ½ cup water to a boil in a medium saucepan; cook, stirring constantly, until sugar dissolves, about 3 minutes. Add strawberries, remove from heat, and let sit 30 minutes to infuse syrup with strawberry flavor. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a small bowl (do not press on solids); cover and chill until cold, about 30 minutes.

Step 3
Scrape rosé into a blender. Add lemon juice, 3½ ounces strawberry syrup, and 1 cup crushed ice and purée until smooth. Transfer blender jar to freezer and freeze until frosé is thickened (aim for milkshake consistency), 25–35 minutes.

Step 4
Blend again until frosé is slushy. Divide among glasses.

Step 5
Do Ahead: Rosé can be frozen 1 week ahead.

Prepare all the ingredients on the counter to be able to work well and quickly, especially the cream and egg white.

Pour all the ingredients into a shaker.

Shake vigorously for 1 minute: cream and egg white must be mixed perfectly, so don't rush.

Now open the shaker and put some ice and shake for 1-2 minutes. It depends on how long you can resist!

Pour into a highball glass, add a splash of soda and garnish to taste.

Ramos Gin Fizz was once drunk as an invigorating drink or even as a breakfast, try it as an aperitif and after dinner and you will discover a little gem now lost.
